title: Putin criticizes 'disregard' for sports ruling with Russia barred from Alberta world juniors
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has condemned what he calls a "disregard for legal norms" in sports after Russia was barred from the world junior hockey championship following a move by the Canadian…

image.caption: Russia was reinstated to International Ice Hockey Federation world championships in a ruling from the Court of Arbitration for Sport last month, but Canada barred Russia players and the IIHF said last week the Russia team would not take part. President Vladimir Putin is pictured at a news conference

blocks.text: Hockey

Russian President Vladimir Putin has condemned what he calls a "disregard for legal norms" in sports after Russia was barred from the world junior hockey championship following a move by the Canadian government to block its team.
Country has called for tourney to be moved from Canada, appealed to IOC to intervene

Russia was reinstated to International Ice Hockey Federation world championships in a ruling from the Court of Arbitration for Sport last month, but Canada barred Russia players and the IIHF said last week the Russia team would not take part.
The CAS ruling overturned a suspension on Russian teams which the IIHF imposed shortly after the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

While speaking with reporters following talks with U.S. President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping on Thursday, Putin mentioned the "non-implementation of the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling" without referencing Canada or hockey by name.
It was, he said, "even worse" than border restrictions in Finland which have kept out Russian athletes in recent days.

"This simply means disregard for legal norms, in this case the norms of international sports law," Putin said from Shenzhen, China. "It is a grave violation of the Olympic Charter and steps in the direction of destroying Olympism as a whole.

blocks.text: “Sport, just like art, should unite people, but it seems as if someone doesn't want this unity but instead wants an exacerbation of a situation of alarm and conflict in the areas of their activities and perhaps in other places."
Russia has previously called for the junior men's worlds to be moved out of Canada and appealed to the International Olympic Committee to intervene. The IOC has yet to do so.

Canada firm in its decision
Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary for sport, told The Canadian Press on Wednesday that Canada would stand by its decision as long as Russia continues its war in Ukraine.
"Like I said in the media recently, if Putin wants to play hockey and [have] his athletes come to Canada, then he needs to get out of Ukraine," van Koeverden said.

blocks.text: Van Koeverden accused Russia of using sport as propaganda and pointed to its annexation of Crimea in 2014, shortly after it hosted the Winter Olympics in Sochi.
"That's not what sport is for, that's not what sport is about, and we won't tolerate it on Canadian soil," he said.

Asked whether Russia could use its appeal to the IOC to jeopardize Canada's chances of hosting future international sporting events, van Koeverden said Canada is "the best sport hosting nation in the world, and people want to come to Canada."
Norway has replaced Russia in the draw for the world juniors in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. from Dec. 26-Jan. 5.
The IIHF did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Putin's remarks.
